n: The congregation gives thanks twice over, because God’s name — his presence — is near, as his wonderful deeds show.
Now God himself speaks: when the time I have set arrives, I will judge with perfect fairness. God, not humans, chooses the moment of justice.

f.w: When I shall receive the congregation
f.g: Better, “When I choose the appointed time.”

n: Even if the earth and its people seem to melt and totter, God holds its pillars steady.

f.w: I bear up the pillars of it

n: God warns the boastful: stop bragging. To the wicked: don’t raise your horn.

f.g: An animal’s horn — a symbol of strength and pride.

n: Don’t lift your horn so high or speak with stubborn arrogance.

f.g: Stubborn pride, like an ox that won’t bend to the yoke.

n: Lifting up — success and honor — doesn’t come from any direction on earth. (The north isn’t mentioned; some think it is left for God’s own dwelling.)
God is the judge: he lowers one person and raises another. True honor comes from him.

f.w: he putteth down one, and setteth up another

n: God holds a cup of foaming, spiced wine — the cup of his judgment. The wicked will have to drink it to the last bitter drop.

f.g: The cup of God’s wrath — a common image of judgment.
The thick sediment at the bottom of a cup.

n: “But I” — the psalmist will declare God’s deeds forever and sing to the God of Jacob.
God will cut off the proud strength of the wicked and lift up the strength of the righteous.

f.w: the horns of the righteous shall be exalted
